title: The Twisted Psychology Of Sovereign Citizens
summary: Walks through six core sovereign-citizen beliefs with traffic-stop and courtroom clips, explains why each fails, and covers the psychology of the appeal.

assertions.quote: Criminal laws, traffic laws, and tax laws can be enforced without the person's consent.
Laws are typically statutory, meaning they apply to everyone within a predetermined jurisdiction, whether they agree or not.
There is no strawman persona or government account that they'll take the money from.
There are no secret bank accounts that will give you access to millions and millions of dollars.
be skeptical of individuals advocating that speeding tickets, summons, bills, tax notifications, or similar documents can be resolved by writing acceptance for value
These documents are then sold to people under the guise that they are kits
the right to travel does not mean the right to operate a motor vehicle without regulation
modern laws define driver as anyone operating a motor vehicle
And this ends in a similar fashion to so many of these encounters.
Simply writing the phrase on a document doesn't make it legally meaningful.

verdicts.note: Duress is a factual defence that must be proven; a notation on a signature does not create it.

assertions.quote: by not declaring themselves as a person, they're outside the jurisdiction of the law. Not true.

verdicts.note: Courts treat every human as a legal person subject to law; the living-man declaration has never succeeded.
